epic.intent:
## Outcome
With the dev3000 capability on, a hosted agent debugging a web app can start the project under dev3000 (d3k) and read one ordered timeline of server output, browser console messages, exceptions and network requests, instead of asking the person to paste logs. The folder page shows whether a d3k session is running and lets the person stop it.

## Confirmed decisions (person, 2026-11-12)
- This epic starts with a bounded investigation on Windows; the rest of the plan is redrafted from its result at the Sprint 1 checkpoint.
- (2026-11-15) Sprint 1 is a spike sprint whose outcome is a properly vetted Sprint 2: real commands, pin and verified source locations, approved at the checkpoint before anything is built.
- Deep integration is the target if the investigation supports it.

## Evidence inspected
- dev3000 0.0.192 on npm (MIT), 2026-11-10. Its README says the new skill-owned runtime is not released yet and must be run from a source checkout; it needs Node.js 24+, pnpm, Chrome and a ready portless HTTPS setup, and uses its own managed Chrome with a per-project profile. Windows support is not stated.
- It tells the agent not to start a second server or browser during a session, which may conflict with the in-app browser pane.

## Scope of Sprint 1
- Establish on this Windows machine what actually works: the npm release versus the unreleased runtime, the portless dependency, Chrome ownership, event reads, redaction, and clean shutdown.
- Decide between three outcomes: integrate now as a capability, integrate a reduced read-only form, or defer until upstream releases.
- Turn the decision into a vetted Sprint 2 (or its removal) for the person to approve.

## Provisional Sprint 2 (rewritten after the checkpoint)
- Register dev3000 as a capability, run and stop a session from the app, deliver agent instructions, and prove an agent reads a real error from the timeline.

## Non-goals
- dev3000's Vercel Sandbox and remote-harness modes (macOS only upstream, cloud accounts).
- Storing timeline content in Dark Mechanicus records; the timeline stays in d3k's memory.
- Replacing the in-app browser pane.
- Native verification on macOS or Linux: no such machine is available to this project today. Those code paths are unit-tested and the runbook says the feature is verified on Windows only.

## Standards
Only the project Definition of Done gates acceptance. Each ticket writes and runs the tests its Tests section lists.

successCriteria.text: A written decision, backed by commands actually run on Windows and their output, states which dev3000 form (npm release, source runtime, or none yet) is usable and why.

If integration proceeds: with the capability on, an agent starts the fixture web app under dev3000 and reads a deliberately triggered browser exception and its preceding server line from the timeline.
If integration proceeds: the folder page shows the running session and Stop ends the dev server, the managed Chrome and the runtime, verified by process listing.
If integration proceeds: nothing from the timeline is written into Dark Mechanicus records or the repository.
If the decision is to defer: the capability is not shipped, and the decision document names the upstream condition that would reopen the work.

epic.title: dev3000: one timeline of server and browser events that hosted agents can read

bundle.rationale:
## Approach
Investigate before committing. dev3000's current runtime is unreleased and its Windows support is unstated, so Sprint 1 is a spike: one bounded investigation that ends in a decision and a vetted Sprint 2 at a human checkpoint. Sprint 2 is written now so the intended shape is visible, and every ticket in it is marked provisional.

## Decisions and why
- **Person's choice (2026-11-15): spike sprint.** This is the one epic where a second sprint is a real human decision, not an arbitrary split: dev3000's runtime is unreleased and Windows support is unstated, so Sprint 2 cannot be planned honestly in advance. The spike's deliverable is a vetted Sprint 2 that the person approves.
- **Person's choice: spike first.** The alternative, planning the full integration against npm 0.0.192, risks building on a form upstream is replacing.
- **The app starts and stops sessions but never reads the timeline.** The timeline can hold request bodies and console output; keeping it out of the app's records avoids a new class of stored sensitive data. Agents read it directly with the tool.
- **Browser ownership rule in the agent paragraph.** The tool says not to run a second browser or server during a session; the paragraph tells agents to use d3k's browser for that app while a session runs.
- **No sandbox or remote modes.** They need macOS and cloud accounts.

## Possible outcomes of Sprint 1 and what each changes
- Integrate now: Sprint 2 is redrafted with the real commands and pin, then runs.
- Reduced: Sprint 2 drops run-from-the-app and keeps install, paragraph and proof.
- Defer: Sprint 2 is removed; the epic completes with the report, and a new epic is planned when the named upstream condition is met.

## Risks
- The tool does not work on Windows: that is a valid Sprint 1 result, not a failure.
- It requires portless HTTPS, which needs the person's system prompt: the entry criteria require the Capabilities epic, which ships portless and its HTTPS setup, to be complete first.
- Orphaned Chrome or dev server: Sprint 2 verifies by process listing.

## Sequencing
Sprint 1 is one ticket. Sprint 2 is a chain: descriptor, session control, then the smoke and the runbook in parallel.

## Dependencies on other epics
Requires the Capabilities epic complete; it ships portless, including the HTTPS setup (the former portless epic was folded into it on 2026-11-15).

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/reports/dev3000-windows.md` answers the eight questions with commands, outputs, dates and the version or commit, each labelled observed, read from source, or unverified.
The report includes process listings before start, while running and after stop.

The report ends with one decision (integrate now, reduced, or defer) and the evidence for it; for integrate, the pin, the commands and the stop procedure; for defer, the upstream condition that reopens the work.
No personal browser profile, account sign-in or system trust change was used; the report says so and shows the profile folder used.

The report ends with a proposed Sprint 2 for the chosen outcome: for integrate or reduced, each ticket's scope, verified source locations, pinned version and re-run commands, tests and size; for defer, the removal and the upstream condition.

tickets.body:
## Context
dev3000 (d3k) 0.0.192 is on npm (MIT). Its README says the new skill-owned runtime is not released and must be run from a source checkout, that it needs Node.js 24 or later, pnpm, Chrome and a ready portless HTTPS setup, and that it uses its own Chrome with a per-project profile. It does not state Windows support.

## Questions to answer, each with the command, its output, the date and the version or commit
1. What does npm 0.0.192 actually provide on Windows: which commands exist and run? Does `npm ci --ignore-scripts` from a pinned lockfile give a working install?
2. Does the source runtime (`skills/d3k/scripts/runtime.mjs` at a pinned commit) start on Windows? Does it require Bun?
3. Is portless HTTPS mandatory, or does any mode work over plain HTTP?
4. With the fixture web app (`scripts/native/fixtures/webapp/`): start a session, load `/boom`, and read the browser exception and the `fixture failure requested` server line with `d3k errors --context --json` and `d3k events`.
5. Which Chrome does it launch, with which profile folder, and can the profile be placed in a folder the app chooses?
6. What does `d3k stop` end? List processes before start, while running and after stop.
7. What persists on disk, and where? Is anything sent off the machine?
8. Does a d3k session conflict with the in-app browser pane showing the same app?

## Decision to write
One of: **integrate now** (name the form, the pin, the commands the app runs, and the stop procedure); **integrate a reduced form** (say what is left out and why); or **defer** (name the upstream condition that reopens the work). Give the evidence for the choice.

## Proposed Sprint 2
The spike's output is a properly vetted Sprint 2, not only a decision. For integrate or reduced, write in the report, for each Sprint 2 ticket: its scope, verified source locations (paths that exist on the branch, with symbols), the pinned version and the exact commands it runs (re-run here), its Tests section and its size. Start from the provisional DM-588 to DM-591 and change, drop or add tickets as the evidence requires. For defer, propose removing Sprint 2 and name the upstream condition.

## Safety
Use a dedicated Chrome profile folder, never the person's everyday profile. Do not sign in to any Vercel account and do not use the sandbox modes. Read prompts before answering; no blind key presses. Do not run the portless HTTPS setup here: use the portless HTTPS setup the Capabilities epic ships, and if HTTPS is required but not set up, stop and record that.

## Source locations (entry points; no code change expected)
- `docs/reports/portless-windows.md` and `docs/runbooks/portless.md` (Capabilities epic, which ships portless).
- `scripts/native/fixtures/webapp/` (Capabilities epic).
- `src/main/panes/browserPane.ts`: the pane the tool may conflict with.
- `docs/reports/omp-cli.md`: report format.

## Tests
None: investigation. The evidence is the report.

reasoning.rationale: Bounded investigation of a pre-release tool that owns a browser and a dev server; ends in a go, reduced or defer decision.

## In scope
- `src/main/capabilities/dev3000/session.ts`: check the preconditions the report names (portless on and, if required, HTTPS set up) and refuse with a reason when unmet; start a session through the managed process service with the profile folder inside the app's private folder when the report says that is possible; report state; stop by the report's procedure and confirm the dev server, the Chrome instance and the runtime are gone.

`session.test.ts`: unmet preconditions refuse with the reason; start is refused while running; stop runs the procedure then the tree kill; state follows a late exit correctly. `CapabilitiesCard.test.tsx`: the row states. Handler tests: untracked folder refused.

Run the tests, lint, typechecks; start and stop the fixture web app session once in a dev build and attach a screenshot.
